claim: In `Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Pointwise/Finset/Basic.lean`, the file this PR edits, the PR removes `noncomputable` from `Finset.monoid` but leaves it on `Finset.commMonoid` (line 939) and on its siblings `Finset.divisionMonoid` (line 964), `Finset.divisionCommMonoid` (line 1020) and `Finset.coeMonoidHom` (line 770). None of the four needs it. So the PR's stated goal, removing `noncomputable` from the Set/Finset Monoid instances, is only half done in this file, and the Finset monoid family is now inconsistent: `Finset.monoid` is computable, but the `CommMonoid`, `DivisionMonoid` and `DivisionCommMonoid` built on the same `coe_injective` pattern are not.
requested_change: Change `protected noncomputable def commMonoid` to `protected def commMonoid`. Make the same change to `Finset.divisionMonoid` and `Finset.divisionCommMonoid`, and change `noncomputable def coeMonoidHom` to `def coeMonoidHom`, so the file has no `noncomputable` left.
evidence: content_search for `noncomputable` under Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Pointwise: the only matches left in the PR state are these four declarations in Finset/Basic.lean. Set/Basic.lean has none. lean_verify_edit replaced lines 770-1022 with the same text minus the four `noncomputable ` keywords and returned success; the line-939-only edit also succeeded. As a control, adding `def testNCControl : ℕ := Classical.choice ⟨0⟩` to the same file failed with "axiom 'Classical.choice' not supported by code generator; consider marking definition as 'noncomputable'". So the verifier does run the code generator, and a successful check means the declaration really is computable. The file compiles as the PR leaves it (as-is check: compiles=true).

claim: `Finset.mulAction` in `Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Action/Pointwise/Finset.lean` (lines 76-87) still carries the same `#adaptation_note /-- nightly-2025-04-07 ... needs to be marked as noncomputable because of its dependence on Set.monoid ... -/` that this PR deletes above `Finset.monoid`, and it is still `protected noncomputable def`. This PR makes `Set.monoid` computable, so the note's stated reason is now false, and the declaration compiles without `noncomputable`. The two notes were added together for the same cause (Zulip, #23806 thread: "I've added adaptation notes to the two `noncomputable`s that were flagged ... in review"). Removing one and leaving the other leaves a stale adaptation note in the library.
requested_change: In `Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Action/Pointwise/Finset.lean`, delete the `#adaptation_note /-- nightly-2025-04-07 ... -/` block (lines 76-81) above `Finset.mulAction`. claim: `Set.mulAction : MulAction (Set α) (Set β)` in `Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Action/Pointwise/Set/Basic.lean` (line 173) is the `Set` twin of `Finset.mulAction`. It sits directly on the `Set.monoid` that this PR makes computable, yet it is still `protected noncomputable def`, and it compiles without the keyword. The same holds for the other pointwise `Set`/`Finset` structures built on the instances this PR touches: `Set.hasDistribNeg` (which uses `Set.involutiveNeg`, made computable here), `Set.distribSMulSet`, `Set.distribMulActionSet`, `Set.mulDistribMulActionSet`, `Finset.distribNeg`, `Finset.distribSMul`, `Finset.distribMulAction`, `Finset.mulDistribMulAction` and `Submodule.pointwiseSetMulAction`. With these left in place, the cleanup of the pointwise `noncomputable`s is incomplete.
requested_change: Change `protected noncomputable def mulAction [Monoid α] [MulAction α β] : MulAction (Set α) (Set β) where` to `protected def mulAction [Monoid α] [MulAction α β] : MulAction (Set α) (Set β) where`. Drop `noncomputable` the same way from the pointwise declarations listed in the claim. If the PR is to stay two-file, open a follow-up that does this instead.
